strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation identifying real limitations (lack of verification/correction) in existing multi-turn Text-to-SQL systems with natural MDP-based solution

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations, multi-dimensional analysis (turns, difficulty, error types, training dynamics), and both in/out-of-domain generalization demonstrating the approach's robustness
Strong empirical results achieving SOTA on CoSQL/SParC with 1.7B and 4B models that outperform larger baselines, suggesting genuine methodological effectiveness
Sophisticated warm-start training pipeline combining self-taught SFT with difficulty-aware reject sampling and well-designed multi-level rewards tailored per action type

weaknesses: Severe latency concerns inadequately addressed: 20-35x increase in inference time (0.8s→16.6s for 1.7B model) and 50x response token explosion fundamentally limit real-world deployment, yet treated as future work rather than core limitation

Extensive experimental analysis across multiple research questions with insightful breakdowns by dialogue turn and query difficulty
Systematic three-stage training pipeline (warm-start SFT with difficulty-aware sampling, curriculum RL, multi-level rewards) with reasonable design
Thorough ablation studies (Table 4) and error type analysis (Figure 7) providing useful diagnostic insights
Strong empirical performance on CoSQL and SParC benchmarks with smaller model sizes (1.7B/4B)

Massive unaddressed practical limitation: ~50x latency overhead (2,380 vs 47 tokens; 16-28s vs 0.8-1.0s) makes approach prohibitive for interactive systems; no token/accuracy trade-off analysis

Critical missing implementation details: memory extraction mechanism (tool-parsed constraints/entities) undefined; Mt-1 update strategy unclear; memory retrieval scalability unknown; reward function weights selected via grid search but not reported; no sensitivity analysis

Incomplete experimental rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing; all results appear to be single runs; Table 7 shows only 81-86% SFT trajectory coverage leaving 14-19% unexplained; Table 3 out-of-domain gains modest (3-5%)

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation clearly identifying short-horizon reasoning limitations in multi-turn Text-to-SQL and proposing principled MDP-based solution
Comprehensive and thoughtfully designed three-stage training pipeline combining self-taught warm-start SFT with difficulty-aware sampling and end-to-end RL with multi-level rewards
Extensive experimental validation with rigorous ablations, in/out-of-domain evaluation, and error analysis demonstrating clear contributions of each component
Strong empirical results achieving SOTA on CoSQL and SParC, with impressive efficiency (1.7B/4B models outperforming 14B+ models and GPT-based approaches)
Larger gains on harder queries and later dialogue turns (Figure 4) provide evidence that long-horizon reasoning addresses key complexity scenarios
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and commitment to reproducibility through promised code/model/trajectory release
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - individual components (MDP formulation, self-taught learning, GRPO, curriculum RL) are established techniques; novelty primarily lies in combination

Reward function design appears ad-hoc: clause-matching F1 choices, binary verification rewards, and weight grid search lack justification; no sensitivity analysis provided

Incomplete failure analysis: no reporting of first-attempt success rates, refinement loop failure modes, max_turns adequacy, or execution verification error rates
Missing ablations on key design choices: curriculum schedule justification, max_turns sensitivity, reward weight sensitivity, and SFT hyperparameter choices

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation: Clear distinction between short-horizon and long-horizon reasoning with explicit MDP formulation addressing real limitations in multi-turn Text-to-SQL coherence and verification

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Four research questions with systematic ablations (EXECUTE/MEMORY-VERIFY necessity, reward components), multi-dimensional analysis (difficulty, turns, generalization), and detailed case studies

Strong empirical results: SOTA on CoSQL/SParC using smaller 1.7B-4B models; substantial improvements on harder queries (+3.8 EX on Turn≥4) and demonstration of robustness across base models and evaluation settings

Thoughtful multi-level reward design: Process rewards tailored to action types (clause-level F1 for PROPOSE/SELF-CORRECT, verification accuracy tables for E/M-VERIFY) provide dense learning signals for hard examples
Self-taught warm-start SFT: Difficulty-aware rejection sampling is creative, improving trajectory coverage from 67.5% to 81% (CoSQL) with explicit handling of easy vs. hard cases
Strong reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters, tool configurations, code availability promised, and use of open-source Qwen models facilitate reproduction
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core components (GRPO, curriculum learning, self-taught learning, rejection sampling) are from prior work; contribution is primarily in application/engineering rather than new methods or algorithms

Unrealistic evaluation setup: Default uses ground-truth SQL from prior turns in dialogue history; Table 6 shows realistic setting with predicted history drops 3.4 EX points (79.9→76.5), making practical validity questionable. Most prior turns use gold SQL

Prohibitive computational cost limits applicability: 28-second latency with up to 1,880 avg. tokens generated; Table 13 shows sharp performance degradation with token limits <4000, forcing users to accept high latency for gains. Applicability to interactive/real-time scenarios unclear
Incomplete training data coverage: Table 9 shows 19.7% (CoSQL) and 13.6% (SParC) of examples lack valid trajectories even after 3 self-taught rounds; impact on final model from this gap not analyzed

Memory module underspecified: Current implementation stores 'parsed constraints as text' but parsing strategy not detailed; no recall/precision analysis of memory retrieval; discussion mentions vector DB but not evaluated; when does memory-verification fail unclear

Process reward design lacks rigor: Hand-crafted E-VERIFY reward mappings (null→0.1, error→1) lack justification; M-VERIFY reward structure unexplained; limited ablation in Table 10 shows process helps (+0.5-0.8 EX) but individual components' contributions unclear; weights via grid search on 'small held-out subset' with no sensitivity analysis

Persistent unresolved error patterns: Aggregation Drift remains largely unsolved (Figure 6); paper acknowledges these are 'extra hard' but provides no analysis of which aggregation patterns cause problems or why the method struggles with them

Modest generalization: Out-of-domain improvements modest (4.8 EX point gap CoSQL→SParC); error propagation with predicted history still 3.4 EX below gold; single-turn evaluation (Table 12) weak vs. specialized models; schema scalability claimed but not empirically validated

Insufficient ablations: No ablation on curriculum learning necessity; no comparison of dialogue memory representations; max_interaction=4 limit not justified; base long-horizon model without training performs extremely poorly (22.6 EX) but root cause unexplored

Statistical rigor gaps: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests reported; some result differences small (77.3 vs 77.6); single-seed training assumed; no sensitivity analysis on critical hyperparameters

strengths: Well-motivated long-horizon formulation that clearly articulates limitations of short-horizon approaches
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with RQ-driven analysis, difficulty-based breakdowns, turn-based analysis, and systematic ablations
Solid empirical results achieving competitive performance with smaller model sizes (1.7B/4B) on CoSQL and SParC
Detailed error taxonomy and case study analysis showing concrete improvements in execution and coherence errors
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 2) and extensive appendix with implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: MDP formulation is straightforward; core contribution reduces to combining existing techniques (self-taught learning, GRPO, tool-use) without methodological innovation

Critical experimental flaw: Main results (Tables 2-3) use gold SQL history from previous turns, not model-generated history; this is unrealistic for real deployment and should disqualify or severely downgrade claims

Insufficient causal analysis: Missing breakdown of improvement sources—unclear how much comes from MDP framework vs. warm-start data vs. GRPO training; base agent performance (22.6% EX) implausibly weak

Severe practical limitations inadequately addressed: 28.3-second latency incompatible with real-time applications; memory design (text-based) unvalidated at scale; schema scalability claimed but not empirically tested

Limited experimental scope: Only two related datasets (CoSQL, SParC); single alternative base model; no statistical significance testing; some improvements modest; missing contemporary baselines and direct comparisons
Reproducibility concerns despite code-release promise: Hyperparameter selection vague ('grid search on small held-out subset'); curriculum design ad-hoc (bin size 2000); sensitivity analyses missing

Incomplete failure mode analysis: Aggregation drift remains unresolved despite long-horizon reasoning; extra-hard cases in Figure 8 show persistent difficulties without explanation of fundamental limits
Weak reward design justification: Clause-match F1 lacks importance-weighting; E-VERIFY rewards appear ad-hoc; process reward gains modest (Table 10), suggesting outcome rewards dominate

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: clearly demonstrates limitations of short-horizon paradigms in multi-turn Text-to-SQL and proposes principled MDP-based solution

Strong experimental results: achieves state-of-the-art on CoSQL/SParC with small models (1.7B/4B), outperforming larger closed-source models; consistent improvements across in-domain, out-of-domain, and robustness settings

Comprehensive evaluation methodology: systematically addresses four research questions (RQ1-RQ4) with thorough ablations, error analysis, generalization tests across base models, and out-of-domain/single-turn evaluation
High reproducibility standards: extensive implementation details, promised recipe release, clear hyperparameters, tool configurations, and algorithm descriptions in appendices
Thoughtful engineering: difficulty-aware trajectory sampling, multi-level reward design (outcome + process), curriculum RL, and discussion of industrial-scale schema/memory scalability
Compelling robustness evidence: Table 6 showing +5.3% margin improvement with model-predicted prior SQL (vs. +4.7% with gold) demonstrates superior verification-and-refinement loop
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in individual components: self-taught learning is bootstrapping, GRPO training follows existing work (Shao et al. 2024), process rewards are standard in semantic parsing RL; main contribution is the combination, which is somewhat incremental

Significant practical limitations: latency ~28 seconds with 8000-token limit severely restricts interactive applications; token cost 38× higher than short-horizon SFT (1880 vs. 49 tokens) makes deployment expensive for low-accuracy-critical scenarios

Narrow evaluation scope: only two closely related datasets (CoSQL, SParC); no evaluation on other conversational semantic parsing tasks; out-of-domain is merely train-one-test-other within same distribution family

Incomplete ablations: missing sensitivity analysis on key design choices (e.g., bin size 2000, 20 rollouts, curriculum boundaries); process reward contributes only +0.6% EX; no ablation isolating execution vs. memory verification on trained model

Memory module underexplored: scalability to long dialogues unclear; current text-based constraint storage is simplistic; no analysis of memory retrieval failures or dialogue-length effects; vector database backend is speculative
Error analysis limitations: relies on 'LLM-as-judge' (GPT-5) for classification without bias discussion; aggregation drift errors remain largely unresolved; error taxonomy has overlapping categories
